<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as mushrooms

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-mushrooms" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-mushrooms-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of mushrooms, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

id="hmi-occurrence-mushrooms-methods" data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:mushrooms-a0d8b45335c0:b49d076cb933"><summary>HMI mushrooms Pb reference · Mushrooms, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:mushrooms-a0d8b45335c0:b49d076cb933"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI mushrooms Pb reference · Mushrooms, as sold. Mushrooms, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤4</td><td>89</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤4</td><td>89</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>175 reference units; 4 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>146</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>27</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>Spungen et al. 2024</td><td>1</td><td>25%</td></tr><tr><td>Unguryanu et al. 2023</td><td>1</td><td>25%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for mushrooms, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>4 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li><li><a href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" class="internal" data-slug="sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" data-no-cite-meta>Spungen et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/unguryanu2023-arkhangelsk-wild-mushrooms-berries-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/unguryanu2023-arkhangelsk-wild-mushrooms-berries-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Unguryanu et al. 2023</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:mushrooms-a0d8b45335c0:b49d076cb933</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Pankavec et al. 2019</td><td>3</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for mushrooms, as sold on a dry weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Pankavec et al. 2019 is the only compatible sampling family for mushrooms, as sold on this basis in the completed mushrooms ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/pankavec2019-pickled-mushrooms-poland-minerals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/pankavec2019-pickled-mushrooms-poland-minerals" data-no-cite-meta>Pankavec et al. 2019</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:mushrooms-37d592edcad1:87064c7b9d70</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach mushrooms

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach mushrooms comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Mushrooms, as sold from substrate amended with 0.4 mM each of As(III), As(V) and DMAA (experiment) had As(III) higher at 3,990 µg/kg, against 260 µg/kg for no arsenic added to substrate (control) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mleczek2016-mushroom-arsenic-substrate|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mleczek M, Niedzielski P, Siwulski M, Rzymski P, Gasecka M, Golinski P, Kozak L, Kozubik T · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mleczek2016-mushroom-arsenic-substrate">Importance of low substrate arsenic content in mushroom cultivation and safety of final food product</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">European Food Research and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mleczek2016-mushroom-arsenic-substrate">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, mushrooms, as sold from production strain 2, substrate sodium selenate 2.0 mg/dm3 Se (Z) (experiment) had Se higher at 810 µg/kg, against 110 µg/kg for production strain 2, substrate control, 0 mg/dm3 Se (C) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/golian2021-oyster-mushroom-strains-metals|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Golian M, Hegedusova A, Mezeyova I, Chlebova Z, Hegedus O, Urminska D, Vollmannova A, Chlebo P · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/golian2021-oyster-mushroom-strains-metals">Accumulation of Selected Metal Elements in Fruiting Bodies of Oyster Mushroom</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2022, 11(1), 76 (published online 29 December 2021)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/golian2021-oyster-mushroom-strains-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that mushrooms, as sold from Large-white carpophores, crude had methylmercury higher at 62.2 µg/kg, against 20.9 µg/kg for All developmental stages combined, braised in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/falandysz2022-boletus-mercury-methylmercury|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Falandysz J, Saba M, Rutkowska M, Konieczka P · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/falandysz2022-boletus-mercury-methylmercury">Total mercury and methylmercury (MeHg) in braised and crude Boletus edulis carpophores during various developmental stages</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/falandysz2022-boletus-mercury-methylmercury">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed mushrooms in the same study and group. Mushrooms, dried (all samples) had lead equal to at 20 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (mushrooms, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|28]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, mushrooms, canned (Addis Ababa sample) had lead lower at 11,700 µg/kg, against 18,000 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (mushrooms, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/woldegiorgis2015-ethiopian-edible-mushrooms-minerals|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Woldegiorgis AZ, Abate D, Haki GD, Ziegler GR · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/woldegiorgis2015-ethiopian-edible-mushrooms-minerals">Major, Minor and Toxic Minerals and Anti-Nutrients Composition in Edible Mushrooms Collected from Ethiopia</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Processing &amp; Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/woldegiorgis2015-ethiopian-edible-mushrooms-minerals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that mushrooms, dried (all samples (4 sampling occasions, composites)) had inorganic arsenic higher at 45 µg/kg, against 5 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (mushrooms, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|30]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mleczek2016-mushroom-arsenic-substrate|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mleczek M, Niedzielski P, Siwulski M, Rzymski P, Gasecka M, Golinski P, Kozak L, Kozubik T · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mleczek2016-mushroom-arsenic-substrate">Importance of low substrate arsenic content in mushroom cultivation and safety of final food product</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">European Food Research and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mleczek2016-mushroom-arsenic-substrate">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

In the studies available, mushrooms from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than mushrooms from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/domagalska2026-poland-dried-mushrooms-toxic-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Domagalska J, Rusin M, Rogala D, Gut-Pietrasz K, Buczkowska M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/domagalska2026-poland-dried-mushrooms-toxic-elements">Evaluation of Toxic Elements in Commercial Dried Mushrooms from the Polish Market: Exposure Assessment and Health Risk Characterization</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2026, 31(11), 1865</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/domagalska2026-poland-dried-mushrooms-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Mushrooms, dried from certified ecological (organic) products, all species had cadmium higher at 950 µg/kg, against 595 µg/kg for all 164 retail dried mushroom samples, Polish market in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/domagalska2026-poland-dried-mushrooms-toxic-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Domagalska J, Rusin M, Rogala D, Gut-Pietrasz K, Buczkowska M · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/domagalska2026-poland-dried-mushrooms-toxic-elements">Evaluation of Toxic Elements in Commercial Dried Mushrooms from the Polish Market: Exposure Assessment and Health Risk Characterization</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2026, 31(11), 1865</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/domagalska2026-poland-dried-mushrooms-toxic-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in mushrooms?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same mushrooms.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|28]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Mushrooms, dried (all samples) had lead equal to at 20 µg/kg, against 20 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (mushrooms, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|28]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-mushrooms-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-mushrooms-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in mushrooms is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in mushrooms is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
